sections.h2: Where does Mackinac County record deeds?
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages and related papers for Mackinac County land are recorded at the Register of Deeds on the first floor of the Mackinac County Courthouse, 100 S. Marley in St. Ignace, MI 49781. The office phone is (906) 643-7306, and the county register of deeds page lists the online index search, fee schedules and exemption lists.

The office keeps records only for parcels inside Mackinac County. A cabin on Mackinac Island, a lot in Moran Township and a house in the city of St. Ignace all record here, but a Cheboygan or Chippewa County parcel does not. The office also administers the real estate transfer tax, so the tax and the deed are handled at one counter.

The county itself is unusual. It covers 2,101 square miles, and 51% of that is water, because it touches both Lake Huron and Lake Michigan at the Straits of Mackinac. The 2020 census counted 10,834 residents, and the county seat is St. Ignace, the northern end of the Mackinac Bridge. Because so much of the county is water and a ferry or bridge crossing separates many owners from the courthouse, the mail and e-recording options below matter.

sections.h2: Do I have to bring the deed to St. Ignace in person?
sections.html:
No. The register of deeds states that documents with the right fee can be submitted by mail, UPS or FedEx, and a self-addressed return envelope is required. Electronic recording also works: the office accepts submissions through CSC E-Recording Solutions, Simplifile and EPN E Recording Partners Network, and each vendor sets its own pricing.

For a seller who lives downstate or out of state, a closing through a title company usually means the e-recording route. For an owner of an island cottage who is closing by mail, the practical steps look like this:

  • Have the deed signed in black or dark blue ink and acknowledged before a notary.
  • Confirm the grantee's mailing address is printed on the deed.
  • Print the drafter's name and address on the document.
  • Include the total fee as one check, plus the transfer tax or a stamp of exemption language on the face of the deed.
  • Add the return envelope so the recorded original comes back to you or your title agent.

The office does not supply deed forms and cannot fill them out for you. Its FAQ points people to an attorney or title company for drafting.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Mackinac County?
sections.html:
Recording a document costs $30.00 regardless of page count, a flat fee set by the Michigan Legislature in MCL 600.2567 that took effect October 1, 2016. A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3.00 for each extra instrument. Certifying a recorded document is $5.00, copies are $1.00 per page, and record searches run 50 cents per year searched with a $5.00 minimum.

A warranty deed or a land contract with a warranty clause needs a treasurer's tax certificate first. That certificate is $5.00 and can be paid in the same check as the recording fee, for $35.00 in total. If you mail the deed to the register's office, staff obtain the certificate from the county treasurer before recording.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax calculated on a Mackinac County sale?
sections.html:
The county tax is $0.55 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, and the state tax is $3.75 for each $500, so the combined rate is $4.30 per $500. The county rate comes from MCL 207.504, which sets 55 cents in counties under 2,000,000 people. The seller or grantor is liable under the state act, MCL 207.523.

On a $200,000 sale there are 400 units of $500. That gives $220 for the county and $1,500 for the state, or $1,720 in all. A $325,000 island or waterfront sale has 650 units, which works out to $357.50 county and $2,437.50 state.

The deed must show the full consideration on its face, or a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit must be filed with it. No filing fee is charged for that affidavit, but the deed must say that one is being filed. Revenue stamps are bought only in the county where the land lies, and a deed covering parcels in two counties must split the price between them.

sections.h2: Which Mackinac County transfers owe no transfer tax?
sections.html:
Several transfers are exempt, and the exemption must be written on the face of the deed. The county list in MCL 207.505 and the longer state list in MCL 207.526 are posted on the register's site. The ones sellers ask about most:

  • Consideration under $100.
  • Mortgages and other instruments given as security, and their discharges.
  • Leases and mineral transfers.
  • Deeds that correct a flaw in title or confirm title already vested.
  • Land contracts, until legal title passes.
  • Court-ordered transfers with no stated price.
  • Foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure under the state act, though a later resale by the foreclosing owner is taxed.

The state act adds two that the county act lacks: a deed from a parent to a child or stepchild, and a deed from a grandparent to a grandchild. If a seller paid the state tax and later believes an exemption applied, MCL 207.523 lets the seller or the buyer who paid on the seller's behalf ask the Department of Treasury for a refund. Ask a title company or attorney before you rely on any exemption.

sections.h2: What makes a deed get rejected at the Mackinac County counter?
sections.html:
The register's own list of common errors names an incorrect fee, a missing drafter, names not typed beneath signatures, and an incomplete notary certificate. A document that is rejected delays closing, so check it against MCL 565.201 before it leaves your hands.

Layout rules are strict. The first page needs a 2.5 inch blank margin at the top and half an inch on the other sides. Type must be at least 10 point in black ink on white paper of 20 pound weight or heavier, on sheets from 8.5 by 11 to 8.5 by 14 inches. The first line must name one recordable event, and a document that claims more than one event is returned. Only the last four digits of a Social Security number may appear.

A deed from a surviving owner needs a certified death certificate recorded first or referenced by liber and page. Court orders must be certified and sealed by the clerk. The county also offers a property fraud alert service: call the register's office and give your name and email, and you are notified when a document is recorded in your name.

sections.h2: How does a Mackinac Island or St. Ignace sale affect recording and tax?
sections.html:
The recorded deed starts the paperwork, and the buyer must also report the transfer to the local assessor within 45 days under MCL 211.27a. After a transfer of ownership, the taxable value resets to the state equalized value in the following year, which can raise the buyer's bill well above what the seller paid. Transfers to a spouse are not treated as a transfer of ownership, and neither are transfers of residential property to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild when the home is not put to commercial use.

Mackinac County has two cities, Mackinac Island and St. Ignace, plus townships such as Moran. If you rent out a seasonal property, note that the statute's definition of commercial purpose leaves out rentals of fewer than 15 days in a calendar year. Ask the county treasurer for the tax certificate and the local assessor for the parcel's current taxable value before you list.

Foreclosure and tax-lien documents are recorded here too. If a house is behind on payments or tied up in an estate, call the register at (906) 643-7306 to confirm what is already on record, then arrange a title search through a title company.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Mackinac County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30.00 per document no matter how many pages, plus $5.00 for the treasurer's tax certificate when the deed has a warranty clause, so $35.00 in one check. Add $3.00 for each extra instrument a single document assigns or discharges.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate transfer tax in Mackinac County?
faqs.a: The seller or grantor pays it under the state transfer tax act. The combined county and state rate is $4.30 for each $500 of value or fraction, so a $250,000 sale produces $2,150 in transfer tax unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: Can I record a Mackinac County deed by mail?
faqs.a: Yes. The register accepts documents by mail, UPS or FedEx with the correct fee and a self-addressed return envelope. It also accepts e-recording from CSC E-Recording Solutions, Simplifile and EPN E Recording Partners Network.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed need a treasurer's tax certificate?
faqs.a: No, if the quitclaim deed has no covenant of warranty. The certificate requirement in MCL 211.135 covers deeds and land contracts that carry warranty language, and the statute exempts quitclaim deeds that contain no covenants of warranty.

faqs.q: Where do I get a copy of a recorded Mackinac County deed?
faqs.a: Request it from the Mackinac County Register of Deeds at 100 S. Marley, St. Ignace, or search the county's online index. Copies are $1.00 per page, certification is $5.00, and searches cost 50 cents per year with a $5.00 minimum.
